Load Clincoo Env Secrets Only on the Server

Do not bundle private keys into client JavaScript. Read secrets only on the server or an edge function.

This article is available in: Indonesia · English

A process.env value without a public prefix can still leak if you import it from a file that ships in the browser bundle. Anyone who opens DevTools Sources can read that string.

In editor.clincoo.buzz, split server and client modules. Clincoo tokens, payment keys, and webhook secrets may be read only in functions that never reach visitors on app.clincoo.buzz.

If the framework marks public variables (VITE_, NEXT_PUBLIC_), treat the values as public. Do not put secrets there even “just for tests”. Local tests still use a Git-ignored .env.

Ask AI to flag every env import in frontend files. Paste the variable list and ask which ones must move to a server endpoint.

Node docs and web.dev security guidance stress this split. One leak in the client bundle forces key rotation in every environment.
